lessons.title: How a seettu works
lessons.summary: Save together and take turns with the pot.

cards.title: Everyone pays, one takes
cards.body: A seettu has a fixed group. Every round (usually monthly) each member pays the same amount and one member takes the whole pot.

cards.title: An example
cards.body: 10 members paying Rs 5,000 a month make a Rs 50,000 pot. The seettu lasts 10 months, and everyone gets the pot once.

cards.title: No interest
cards.body: If everyone pays, you get back exactly what you put in. A seettu doesn't grow your money; it changes when you have it.

quiz.question: 8 members each pay Rs 2,500 a month. How big is each pot?
If everyone pays every round, how much do you get back in total?
options: More than you paid, with interest
quiz.explanation: A seettu pays no interest: total in equals total out.

quiz.question: How long does a 12-member monthly seettu run?
quiz.explanation: One round per member, so 12 rounds.

lessons.title: Early turn or late turn?
lessons.summary: A loan, or savings without interest.

cards.title: Early turn = a loan
cards.body: Take the pot first and you get a lump sum now, then repay it over the following rounds. It's like an interest-free loan from the group.

cards.title: Late turn = savings
cards.body: Take the pot last and you've lent to everyone else. You save in a disciplined way, but earn no interest while inflation eats into the pot's value.

cards.title: Bidding for turns
cards.body: Some seettus let members bid: whoever gives up the most of the pot goes first, and the rest share that discount. That discount is really interest.

quiz.question: Taking the first pot is most like…
quiz.explanation: You get the money first and repay it over the remaining rounds.

quiz.question: What does a late turn cost you, even if everyone pays?
options: Interest you could have earned elsewhere, and inflation
quiz.explanation: Your money waits without interest while prices rise.

quiz.question: In a bidding seettu, what is the discount someone gives up to go first?
options: Effectively interest paid to the others
quiz.explanation: Paying to get money earlier is what interest is.

cards.title: The classic risk
cards.body: A member takes their pot early and then stops paying. Every later pot shrinks, and nothing is insured.

cards.title: Who you join matters
cards.body: Seettus with people you know and can find are much safer than groups of strangers. In the trainer, a circle of strangers is far more likely to have a member stop paying.

cards.title: Keep records
cards.body: Agree the rules in writing: amounts, dates, the order of turns and what happens if someone misses a payment. Pay by traceable transfer and note who confirmed it.

cards.title: Keep your promise
cards.body: You must keep paying after your pot too. The trainer only lets you join if your wallet could cover every round you owe, even if your pot comes late.

quiz.question: What is the main risk in a seettu?
options: A member who has taken their pot stops paying
quiz.explanation: Seettus run on trust; a member who stops paying shrinks later pots.

quiz.question: Which group is usually safer?
options: People you know and can verify
quiz.explanation: Knowing and being able to find members makes defaults less likely and easier to resolve.

quiz.question: After you've received your pot, should you keep paying?
options: Yes — every member pays every round
Only if you feel like it
quiz.explanation: The others are counting on your payments for their pots.
